args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Its staging build, v2.3.1-rc, was also unhealthy. Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident for it.

- **What was wrong:** the latest deploy, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west and failing health checks, with an 18% error rate. Its test build in staging (v2.3.1-rc) had also been marked unhealthy.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Since v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before, this didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open as a SEV2 for checkout-api, and the on-call engineer has been paged. It covers the failure, the rollback and the current healthy state, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again.
